submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a detector for a learned lexical family of concrete element/substance/technology nouns and their capitalized, name-like forms (wind, water, ice, sand, glass, air, ground, ash, thunder, lightning, flood, oxygen, health, internet; Med, Ind, Inf, Ins, Gl, Rad, Ash, Ded, Brid, Fen, Sand, Thunder, Chris, electr, integ, Wind, Water, Clean, Red, G, GE, MS, Boston, Chris, Barack, Windows, Internet, Data, Health, Land, Environment, East, Access), plus a few short openers (due, come, came, comes, along, across, and up in 'up to'/'up front'): it fires when such a word is the opening fragment of a word GPT-2 splits into several tokens (Wind|shield, Wind|mill, Water|fall, Fire|fighter, Sand|box, Med|ication, Gl|ucose, Inf|rared, Ind|oor, Ash|okan, Ded|ication, Brid|geway, Sand|pipers, Fen|way, Thunder|bolt, Chris|topher, electr|ified, integ|rated, hy|g|ienic) or a single-character piece inside one (Brid|g|eway, hy|g|ienic, glow|-|worms, G|-|d, H|-|Diplo), and on the family's capitalized standalone forms, Wind/wind and due in any context (1.2-3.1). It is near zero on the same compound written as one token (windshield, medication, glucose, indoor, sandbox, waterfront), on the completion pieces of split words (shield, mill, oor, ications, way, bolt), on ordinary concrete nouns and rare words outside the family (stone, river, table, window, house, book, city, money, zeugma), and on its lowercase material words in plain singular use (water, ice, sand, glass, air, ground, ash), which only reach a weak 0.5-1.1 band.

rival_explanations: The pole is simply a token-identity detector for the ~200 token strings in the confound table, so any other capitalized split word (Photos|ynthesis, Snow|board, Black|board, River|bank) should fire on its first fragment just as hard as Med, Inf and Sand do.

The pole fires on the material/natural-element and technology semantics of the word regardless of how GPT-2 tokenizes it, so single-token forms such as windshield, medication, sandbox, snowfall, waterfront and indoor should activate as strongly as their capitalized split forms.

The pole fires only at the opening of a fixed multi-word unit, so the family's words should go silent in plain noun use (e.g. 'It was Wind that broke the fence', 'the Wind case', 'the wind from the sea') and ' up' should fire only in 'up to'/'up front'.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the same compound written as one token (windshield) in ordinary use, which the hypothesis says is near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She dissolved the medication in a glass of water and went to bed early, hoping the headache would fade by morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests single-token medication (near zero by the hypothesis) together with lowercase glass and water in plain singular use (weak 0.5-1.1 band).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The nurse checked his glucose after lunch and wrote the number on the chart again before the evening round.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests single-token glucose, which the hypothesis lists among the one-token compounds it says are near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The children played in the sandbox while their parents talked on the porch and watched the street.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The waterfront was crowded with tourists taking photos of the old harbor and the fishing boats.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests single-token waterfront, where the hypothesis says water semantics in one token stay near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The indoor pool was closed for repairs all week, the manager explained to the waiting guests.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The snowfall kept the plows busy on the highway until well after midnight, the drivers said.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests snow|fall, a split word whose opening fragment snow is a natural element outside the enumerated family, so the hypothesis predicts near zero while rival 2 predicts material semantics.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The water in the lake was cold, so we stayed near the shore and watched the ducks.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests lowercase water in plain singular use, which the hypothesis puts in the weak 0.5-1.1 band rather than active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ice on the pond cracked under the weight of the sled and the children laughed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests lowercase ice in plain singular use, predicted weak and therefore inactive by the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ash from the fireplace covered the ground near the hearth before anyone noticed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests lowercase ash and ground together in plain use, both predicted to reach only the weak band.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They sand the wooden floors for hours before applying the first coat of varnish.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Changes the trigger's part of speech: sand as a verb, where the hypothesis's noun family and weak singular-noun band do not apply.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The landlord will air the apartment before the new tenants move in on Friday.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bolt on the gate had rusted, so he oiled it and tightened the nut with care.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The final score is up to the coach, who has not decided on the lineup yet.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You have to pay up front if you want the discount, the clerk said at the counter.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The label on the bottle read Water, and nothing else was printed on it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests Water as a capitalized standalone family form, which the hypothesis predicts fires regardless of the surrounding phrase.
